newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate drops to 11.4 from 12.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate drops to 11.4 from 12.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dropped to 11.4 percent on Thursday from 12.6 percent in slower trade and amid abundant supply of kuna funds.
Daily settlements totalled a modest 32.4 million kuna, against 48 million kuna on offer.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 27.5 million kuna, mostly granted at a steady call money rate of 10.5 percent.
One-month placements were struck at 14 and 16 percent.
Insurers charged nine percent for old money and banks extended previous term loans at 15 and 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates weaker at 6.1373 against the dollar and at 3.574 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
